releases_reviewed.body:
## 🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under [Bun](https://bun.com). Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the `--bun` flag, because without it `bunx playwright test` runs on Node.js:

```bash
bunx --bun playwright test
```

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

- There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and `--only-changed` does not follow imports.
- Bun loads modules itself, so `--tsconfig` and the JSX options in `tsconfig.json` have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
- Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: `click` instead of `locator.click`. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
- Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

## 🚨 Reports with only failures

New [`failures`](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#failures-reporter) reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New `onlyFailures` option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters [keeps only](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#report-only-failures) tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

```js
// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
  reporter: [
    ['failures'],
    ['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
  ],
});
```

## 🎯 Test runner

- New built-in `-exclusive-` [test lock](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-parallel#test-locks) runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

  ```js
  test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
    // No other test runs while this one is running.
  });
  ```

- [test.skip()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-skip), [test.fixme()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-fixme), [test.fail()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-fail) and [test.slow()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-test#test-slow) now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

  ```js
  test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
    test.skip('Not implemented yet');
  });
  ```

- New `PLAYWRIGHT_TRANSFORM_CACHE_DIR` environment variable sets the directory for transpiled test files, for example on a Linux machine shared with other users.

## New APIs

- New options [`timeout`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send-option-timeout) and [`signal`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send-option-signal) in [cdpSession.send()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession#cdp-session-send).
- New [testRun.mode()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testrun#test-run-mode) returns the execution mode of a suite during [reporter.preprocess()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-reporter#reporter-preprocess).

## Notable Changes ⚠️

- TypeScript class fields now follow [`useDefineForClassFields`](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-typescript#tsconfig-class-fields) from your `tsconfig.json`, the same as `tsc`. It is enabled for `ES2022` and later targets, and when `target` is not specified. A field initializer that reads a constructor parameter property now fails, because the initializer runs first:

  ```js
  class LoginPage {
    // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getByRole')
    readonly submit = this.page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' });

    constructor(private readonly page: Page) {}
  }
  ```

  Move the initialization to the constructor, or set `"useDefineForClassFields": false` in your `tsconfig.json`.

- Actions such as [locator.click()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click), [locator.check()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-check), [locator.tap()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-tap), [locator.fill()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-fill), [locator.clear()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-clear) and [locator.selectOption()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-select-option) now wait for the element to be [not inert](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability#not-inert). An action on an element with the `inert` attribute, or inside such an element, now times out if the element stays inert.

- A sharded run now fails with "No tests found" when no tests match across all shards. Pass `--pass-with-no-tests` to allow this. An empty shard still passes when other shards have tests.

- Cookie matching now follows RFC 6265. With a URL, [browserContext.cookies()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browser-context-cookies) and [apiRequestContext.cookies()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext#api-request-context-cookies) no longer return host-only cookies for subdomains or `Path=/api` cookies for `/apiv2`, and a `Path=/foo/` cookie does not match `/foo`. [APIRequestContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext) sends a cookie without a name as `Cookie: x` instead of `Cookie: =x`, and stores `Set-Cookie: token` as a cookie without a name.

- Proxy credentials are no longer sent to websites. The credentials in the [`proxy`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsertype#browser-type-launch-option-proxy) option now answer only proxy challenges. To authenticate on a website, use [`httpCredentials`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browser#browser-new-context-option-http-credentials).

- Text that the browser does not render, such as text that is not assigned to a slot or text directly inside a closed `<details>`, is no longer part of accessible names and aria snapshots. This can change the results of [page.getByRole()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-role) with a name, [locator.ariaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-aria-snapshot) and [expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot()](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locatorassertions#locator-assertions-to-match-aria-snapshot).

- String and `URLSearchParams` values of the `params` option in [APIRequestContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-apirequestcontext) requests are now appended to the query that the URL already has, instead of replacing it.

- `.css`, `.less` and `.scss` imports in test files now load as empty modules instead of being removed, so the imported file must exist.

- The blob reporter again deletes the content of its output directory before it writes the report. Playwright 1.64 kept reports with other names.

- Test locations of imported calls such as `test(` in CommonJS output now point to the start of the callee, for example `a.spec.ts:3:7` instead of `a.spec.ts:3:11`. This is the same as in ESM.

## Announcements

* ⚠️ Playwright no longer tests on Node.js 20. Use Node.js 22, 24 or 26, as listed in the [system requirements](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro#system-requirements).
* 🐳 [Docker images](https://playwright.dev/docs/docker) now include Node.js 26 instead of Node.js 24, and the latest patch of Chromium on the same branch.

## Browser Versions

- Chromium 158.0.8127.18
- Mozilla Firefox 159.0
- WebKit 27.2

This version was also tested against the following stable channels:

- Google Chrome 157
- Microsoft Edge 156

### Bug Fixes

- #43247 [Bug]: _electron.launch intermittently loses a packaged app's first window since 1.64.0
- #43242 [Regression]: Chromium 155+ aborts a preflighted cross-origin redirect whenever any route is registered (net::ERR_ABORTED)

releases_reviewed.body:
Build input, not a browser download. Nothing here is meant to be installed.

`fonts-bundle-v4.tar.xz` is the font bundle the build stages into every package
(1532 files). `scripts/data/font-bundle.json` pins the asset name, size and
sha256, and `scripts/fetch-fonts.py` verifies it, so a truncated or substituted
download fails loudly.

    sha256  cb7cab7061843e00817af98983c35b3b3fc6092563e29944d9cb878f09c5bf92
    size    896100416

Changes since v1 (v2 and v3 were never published):
- Added Windows faces measured on stock Windows 11: Cascadia Code / Cascadia Mono
  (Windows copies), Dubai Light / Medium, Franklin Gothic Medium Cond,
  Lucida Sans (4 faces), SimSun-ExtG.
- Wingdings, Wingdings 2/3, Symbol, Webdings and Arial Rounded MT Bold now serve
  Windows identities as well as macOS (same bytes on both).
- The Linux/macOS Cascadia copies no longer serve Windows identities.
- `000_README.txt` and `cleanfonts.sh` are no longer in the archive; see `docs/FONTS.md`.

No Adobe fonts: Adobe permits no redistribution, and they were removed in v1.

Tags matching `font-bundle-*` start no workflow.

Bundles uBlock Origin 1.75.0.

## What's Changed
* Release: run the publish jobs past a job their channel skips by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/814
* Release: pass npm publish a local path by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/816
* Release: publish each registry only when its package changed by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/817
* Make GeoIP AIO the default source, deprecate GeoLite2 by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/820
* Fix fill() change events (#825) and proxy credential encoding (#823), guard explicit locales (#824) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/827
* Fix npm `camoufox fetch` failing with EXDEV, and gate merges on a real package install by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/828
* Fix Windows + Python 3.13+: model and GeoIP files installed by one account unreadable by another by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/829
* npm: adm-zip 0.6.1 (three high advisories), and document `npx @camoufox/camoufox` by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/831
* Update vendored cursory-js to 2.0.2 by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/833
* Retry a TypeScript download whose connection drops before any response by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/834
* Keep config keys that older libraries send declared in properties.json by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/836
* Install the paired browser on first launch, and refuse a browser the library cannot drive by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/837
* Publish the npm package as `camoufox` instead of `@camoufox/camoufox` by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/838
* Split the repo into browser/, python/ and typescript/, and fix version pinning (#843) and the WebGL renderer pair (#839) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/846
* Install the camoufox package before the release's font check by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/848
* Hide Juggler from pages, and show them an official Firefox build by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/852
* Date fpgen's model within signed 32-bit time, so read-only Lambda launches work by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/856
* Launch, click and type through each installed package in the install gate by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/859
* Keep pages rendering when another window covers their browser window (#804) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/861
* Release on a twice-monthly train instead of on every merge by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/864
* Behave as on an IPv4-only network when the host's IPv6 disagrees with geoip by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/857
* Validate IP addresses with standard library parsers instead of regex by @RinZ27 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/866
* Stop Xvfb when the process that launched it dies (#868) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/869
* Read response bodies sent with Content-Encoding: identity (#867) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/870
* Give exit-IP lookups through a proxy 15 seconds by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/906
* Update vendored cursory-js to 2.1.0 (Cursory 2.1.0) by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/911
* Test the commit the run started on, in every job by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/876
* Let a re-run job's result replace the first attempt's by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/878
* Stop the virtual display when a Python launch fails by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/908
* Add headless="virtual-gpu": render on a named GPU with no monitor attached by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/912
* Update to Firefox 158.0 by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/914
* Wait thirty seconds for Xvfb to report its display by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/884
* Report leftover browsers and full guard output by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/880
* Give packaged font files ASCII names by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/882
* Give a worker's OffscreenCanvas its context's font list by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/898
* Download the default addons once under concurrent launches by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/902
* Derive a context's appVersion from its own user agent by @coffeegrind123 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/892
* Run ci/tests as a first attempt on a re-run job by @JWriter20 in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/925
* fix(ts): safely resolve maxmind reader constructor using official Reader import by @eduardotashiro in https://github.com/daijro/camoufox/pull/874

recent_changes_reviewed.message:
verify-fonts: check aliases per OS version, and run it on pull requests (#1036)

#997 made an alias name (a macOS TTC weight such as "Noto Sans Canadian
Aboriginal Regular") part of an OS version's base only where that version
has the alias's target, and took it off the always-reported list. The
verifier still required every live alias on that list, so the release
failed before building on macOS's Canadian Aboriginal alias, which only
Sonoma reports, with its target.

The check now asks what the launcher reports: every OS version that
reports an alias's target (its base plus the essentials) must report the
alias, and no optional font group may add a target on its own.

verify-fonts.py ran only in the release, so the pull request that broke it
merged green. build-tester now runs it with --quick on the fonts its
browser artifact carries.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

driven-move-coalescing: pin the display scale and expect device pixels (#1035)

The guard launched a random Linux identity and expected the page to read
the exact CSS point move() was given. A pointer sits on whole device pixels,
so when the identity drew a fractional devicePixelRatio the page read the
nearest one: at 1.25, (415, 226) is device pixel (519, 283), read back as
(415.2, 226.4), as from a real mouse. That failed the release run on main.

The guard now runs at a scale of 1.25 every time, in a window that fits a
1080-pixel display at that scale, and expects the nearest device pixel.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

cpu-vendor-estimates: compute as Intel or AMD x86-64 on an ARM64 host (#1034)

* cpu-vendor-estimates: compute as Intel or AMD x86-64 on an ARM64 host

general.cpu_identity 1 or 2 on an aarch64 build now gives what Firefox's
x86-64 build gives on that vendor's AVX2 and FMA CPU, the reverse of the
ARM64 emulation on x86-64:

- Skia, Web Audio, the speex resampler and libopus compile their x86 paths
  for aarch64 against third_party/simde/x86emu, SIMDe's intrinsics with
  x86's default NaN, NaN operand order and out-of-range conversions. Skia
  and libopus keep the recorded vendor estimate tables.
- ffvpx's FFT runs its x86-64 AVX2/FMA3 assembly translated to C by
  browser/scripts/x86toc.py.
- The JIT, the interpreter, constant folding and Math make x86's negative
  default NaN, and wasm relaxed SIMD gives the x64 backend's lanes
  (JS::SetEmulateX86).

The cpu-vendor-estimates guard now runs on an ARM64 host too, checking the
Intel and AMD launches against stock x86-64. On an Apple M4 (Linux
container) both match in all 46 probe keys that split the architectures,
plus canvas and Opus; on a Ryzen 9850X3D the ARM64 leg still matches.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Regenerate the Math.cpp hunks in patch-apply order

cpu-vendor-estimates.patch applies before windows-crt-math.patch, but its
Math.cpp hunks were written against a tree that already had the CRT patch,
so three hunks were rejected on a clean `make dir`. Each patch's Math.cpp
section is now the diff from the tree its predecessors leave; the resulting
file is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

changes_since_previous_review.message:
Report WebGL2's value for every parameter WebGL1 shares (#1020)

* Report WebGL2's value for every parameter WebGL1 shares

Firefox 156+ creates WebGL1 on WebGL2's GL profile, so every parameter
both contexts report is one driver value. fpgen recorded Firefox 146,
which put WebGL1 on a compatibility profile, and the launchers already
copied WebGL2's line width range over WebGL1's for that reason. Two
Linux records (GeForce GTX 480 and 980) also differ in
ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE, which CreepJS checks: it flags any mirrored
WebGL1/WebGL2 parameter that differs, except the version strings and
the line width range.

The copy now covers every shared non-string parameter, in both
launchers. A test checks every recorded device.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* webgl: test every shared parameter in TypeScript; record the rule's new scope

The TypeScript test still checked only the line width range, so the
launcher's new copy of every shared parameter had no TypeScript test: the
new one walks every recorded GPU and fails on main for the Linux GTX 480
(ALIASED_POINT_SIZE_RANGE). The Python line-width test is covered by the
every-parameter one and goes. webgl-browser-owned-values-follow-firefox
now says WebGL1 takes WebGL2's value for every parameter both report, with
the GTX 480/980 records as evidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Jake Writer <jake_writer@jobharvest.com>

Keep a routed request's header order on the wire (#989)

* Keep original header order when routing

Resuming an intercepted request rebuilds the Firefox channel, losing the order captured at http-on-modify-request. Record that order and merge route overrides back into it, including headers supplied to route.continue_(headers=...). Add document and fetch wire-order tests that compare routed requests with unrouted ones.

* ci: re-run after an unrelated flaky parity test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Drop the unused header-order fallback; test a plain continue with a custom header

Every request records its original header order in the constructor, so
orderRequestHeaders never ran without one: the fallback, its lateNames
argument and DEFAULT_REQUEST_HEADERS were dead. The fetch test now sends a
header of its own and covers route.continue_() with and without headers,
the case the fix is for; both fail on main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Jake Writer <jake_writer@jobharvest.com>

humanize: leave the page straight across the edge, 3px from the last move (#1026)

The exit point lay on the curve's next step, at least 2px from the last
mousemove as Juggler measured it. The page measures from pixels Gecko
rounded, and with the content's top at a fraction (85.5 on some hosts'
toolbars) it saw the two 1.4px apart, closer than any stock exit, and
humanize-mouse-trajectory.py failed now and then in CI.

The exit now leaves straight across the edge it crosses from the pixel the
page last saw, 3px on, which a 1px rounding error keeps at least 2px apart.
The guard also sweeps with text scaled to 105%, which puts the content's
top at 85.5 and failed every run before the change.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bundle a committed uBlock Origin release, not AMO's newest (#1012)

* Bundle a committed uBlock Origin release, not AMO's newest

uBO 1.76.0 reached AMO and changed what pages observe: in every tab
after the first, RegExp moved after URL in the page's global order,
where stock 158 and 159 (every tab and window), no uBO and uBO 1.75.4
keep it after Number. main-world-eval-globals.py caught it, and
534430e0 then took the first tab out of the comparison, which hides
the difference instead of removing it.

fetch-ubo.py resolve now reads browser/scripts/data/ubo.json (1.75.4,
sha256-pinned); `newest` prints AMO's latest as a candidate, so a bump
is a reviewed commit. main-world-eval-globals.py compares the first
tab again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe the bundled uBlock Origin as the committed pin everywhere

README.md, ci/README.md, release.yml, package.py and ci/release.py still
said every package bundles AMO's newest uBO, and release.py that the pin is
in no commit. It is now browser/scripts/data/ubo.json.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Jake Writer <jake_writer@jobharvest.com>

Canvas and Opus follow a claimed CPU vendor (Intel/AMD); vendor joins the fingerprint (#1024)

* Canvas: reproduce Intel's or AMD's RCPPS/RSQRTPS, chosen per identity

Skia's raster pipeline uses x86's estimate instructions for the
non-separable and dodge/burn blend modes, perspective and matrix
inversion. Intel and AMD implement them with different tables (the same
across each vendor's generations and OSes), so canvas readback shows the
host's CPU vendor.

- cpu-vendor-estimates.patch: pref gfx.skia.cpu_vendor_estimates
  (0 host, 1 Intel, 2 AMD). When it names the other vendor, rcp_approx
  and rsqrt_approx in the HSW and SSE paths compute that vendor's bits
  from a recorded table (SkCpuEstimates.h, SkCpuEstimateTables.h).
- browser/tests/cpu-estimates: records each vendor's table and checks the
  emulation against the native instruction over all 2^32 inputs, and
  against the other vendor's recorded hashes.
- Launcher (Python and TypeScript): cpu_vendor option and cpu:vendor key.
  The identity derives it from the GPU where only one vendor carries that
  GPU, and otherwise draws it at Firefox's x86 share (81.4% Intel). A
  coherence rule warns when the two disagree. Apple Silicon gets none.
- Guard cpu-vendor-estimates: stock Firefox 159 hashes from an Intel and
  an AMD CPU; the build matches each when told to.

Audio is not affected: its render splits x86-64 from ARM64, not Intel
from AMD.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Opus: encode with the claimed CPU vendor's RCPPS/RSQRTPS; add the CPU probe

libopus's PVQ search (celt/x86/vq_sse2.c) uses the same two estimate
instructions as Skia, so a WebCodecs, MediaRecorder or WebRTC Opus stream
showed the host's vendor: stock Firefox 159 gives one byte stream on Intel
and another on AMD. libopus lives in libgkcodecs, which cannot read prefs,
so Gecko hands it the table gfx.skia.cpu_vendor_estimates selects
(opus_mozilla_set_cpu_estimates) before each encoder is created, and the
SSE2 search computes the estimates from it lane by lane.

The guard now also encodes one second of Opus and checks it against both
vendors' stock streams, on a secure page since WebCodecs needs one. It
passes on an AMD host for both vendors.

browser/tests/cpu-probe/ is the probe that found it: Math, DOMMatrix,
layout, canvas, WebGL, relaxed SIMD, Web Audio and WebCodecs, with stock
Firefox 159 results from Intel and AMD on Linux and Windows and from an
Apple M4 on macOS and Linux. Intel and AMD differ only in the six
estimate-based composite operations and Opus; ARM64 differs in much more,
which docs/HOST-PARITY.md now lists as not emulated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* cpu:vendor: a core count only Intel ships implies Intel

No AMD x86 CPU since 2015 reports 10, 14, 18, 22 or 28 logical cores:
AMD runs one or two threads per core, and its one-thread parts have 2 to 8
cores. Intel's hybrids report all of them (Core Ultra 5 225, 245K, 125H,
155H; i7-14700K). So an identity with such a hardwareConcurrency is drawn
Intel, and a cpu_vendor='amd' beside it is reported and repaired.

The GPU still decides first: a Radeon APU beside an Intel-only count keeps
AMD and is reported, since no vendor matches both. The rule is renamed
cpu-vendor-matches-hardware. The counts live in launcher-constants.json
(intelOnlyCoreCounts) for both launchers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* cpu {arch, manufacturer}: ARM64 emulation on x86 alongside Intel/AMD

The fingerprint's CPU is now { arch: "x86" | "arm", manufacturer } instead
of a bare vendor, validated per OS (launcher-constants cpuManufacturers):
e.g. Apple + x86 or AMD on macOS is rejected, as is a GPU that never sits
beside the claimed CPU. general.cpu_identity = 3 makes an x86 build compute
what Firefox's aarch64 build computes:

- Skia: the NEON raster pipeline and blend kernels, emulated lane for lane
  (SkOpts_neonemu, SkNeonEmu.h, SkArmEstimates.h).
- Opus: the aarch64 CELT kernels and the NEON inverse MDCT (celt_neonemu.c,
  celt_tx_neonemu.c, translated from celt_tx_neon.S by scripts/a64toc.py),
  for decode and encode.
- WebAudio / wasm / NaN payloads follow the ARM rules.
- libvpx: Firefox configures libvpx realtime-only for linux/arm64 and
  win/aarch64 (not mac/arm64), which changes WebCodecs VP9 output and
  rejects quality-mode VP8. The ARM64 configs are now the full encoder and
  realtime-only is a runtime switch (media.libvpx.realtime_only), so either
  build can produce either result. libvpx NEON itself is bit-exact with x86.

The launchers (Python and TypeScript) set general.cpu_identity and, for an
ARM Windows/Linux identity, media.libvpx.realtime_only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ARM64 identity: make the guard's probe reproducible, fail loudly in ffvpx

The guard served only the probe's own files, so the two webfonts 404ed and
the layout step threw. The probe page draws every input from one seeded
stream, so the throw shifted every later key and made wasm relaxed SIMD and
the convolver look wrong. The fonts now ship beside the probe (both freely
licensed, from Firefox's layout reftests), and the guard fails on any probe
step that errors where stock does not.

Canvas text is rasterized at the identity's devicePixelRatio, which the
launcher draws, so the guard leaves it out; at a ratio of 1 it matches the
M4's.

FFVPXRuntimeLinker asserts that libmozavutil exports the ARM64 switch
instead of skipping it silently. cpu:vendor is kept in properties.json as
removed, and the tribal rule, docs and the constants test follow the
general.cpu_identity pref.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

releases_reviewed.body:
## CloakBrowser Pro: Stable advances to Chromium 156.0.8078.47.1 (all platforms)

Chromium `156.0.8078.47.1` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64), **Windows** (x64), and **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel).

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new

- **The newest Chromium, 156**, on every platform.
- **License connection that finds another way through.** When a license call can't get through, each retry now takes a different route to our servers instead of repeating the same one. This covers launch, heartbeat, and close. Seats are also released more reliably on close.
- **Real window geometry.** The window, the page viewport, and the window position match a real maximized Chrome window for the Windows and macOS personas, in both headed and headless. The viewport is a bit shorter than before, so check scripts that rely on fixed screen coordinates.
- **WebRTC through your SOCKS5 proxy.** With `geoip=True`, WebRTC traffic goes through your SOCKS5 proxy when the proxy supports UDP.
- **Popup blocking and navigation limits stay on**, as in real Chrome, even when an automation tool asks to turn them off.
- **A much more convincing macOS persona** on Linux, and **closer to real Chrome everywhere**: canvas (including inside workers), graphics card names, math, and Windows colors and fonts. On Linux, install the Mac fonts for the macOS persona.
- **New flag `--fingerprint-max-touch-points=<N>`** to report a touch screen, like a Windows touch laptop.
- **On Windows and macOS, this also brings what Linux Stable already had:** the more resilient license connection, request interception that no longer crashes the network process, more Windows fonts, correct Web Audio speed, and Google as the default search engine (`--fingerprint-search-engine=google|bing|duckduckgo|none`).

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

### Current wrapper: v0.7.0

Update the wrapper before launching:

```bash
pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.7.0
```

### Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Stable build for your platform:

```bash
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=155.0.8059.39.2   # Linux
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=155.0.8059.39.1   # Windows, macOS
```

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

**If you hit a regression, please tell us.** [Open an issue](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/issues) or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.

### Checksums (SHA-256)

```text
version=156.0.8078.47.1
46f8361deb898019ef1a529da22b2c9a8f0e482c7a29600b39d932249c84a4b2  cloakbrowser-linux-x64.tar.gz

74dd15bd8af28704f52e23ad55145c0b8c83ffeab4d9283a1779d89bd8bcc434  cloakbrowser-windows-x64.zip
c29ba20dfe53b048760ebccb9a816eda08d0424e430208000d01d7bb216197c8  cloakbrowser-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
1a260c6d31e26695f321a143977b175e7a72295357949da445e7a7a3a384bb5e  cloakbrowser-darwin-x64.tar.gz
```

The signed manifest (`SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig`) is attached. The wrapper verifies its Ed25519 signature and each archive's SHA-256 checksum automatically.

## CloakBrowser Pro: Linux Stable advances to Chromium 155.0.8059.39.2

Chromium `155.0.8059.39.2` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64). Windows and macOS Stable stay on `155.0.8059.39.1`.

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new since 155.0.8059.39.1 (Linux)

- **A more resilient license connection.** Launch and close now ride out brief network or server hiccups by retrying, and startup is a bit quicker. Seats are also released more reliably when you close the browser.
- **Request interception that holds up.** Using `page.route` or other request interception no longer randomly crashes Chrome's network process.
- **More Windows fonts.** Windows personas on Linux now include more app fonts, plus language-pack fonts that follow the locale. A fixed Windows seed will report more fonts than before.
- **Audio at the right speed.** Web Audio now plays at the correct speed on 44.1 kHz and 96 kHz audio devices, and a page's own sample rate is respected.
- **Closer to real Chrome.** The reported window position stays inside the screen's work area, a short GPU vendor flag such as `intel` reports the full vendor name, and one more popular fingerprint test now passes.
- **Google is the default search engine again** when you use the browser directly. Choose another with `--fingerprint-search-engine=google|bing|duckduckgo|none`, or pass your own search URL.

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

### Current wrapper: v0.6.4

Update the wrapper before launching:

```bash
pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.6.4
```

### Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Linux Stable build:

```bash
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=155.0.8059.39.1
```

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

**If you hit a regression, please tell us.** [Open an issue](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/issues) or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.

### Checksums (SHA-256)

```text

f9a2e4666de97f98e3bfdb5d96f9c3c32ae2aa09573b811226a3ddbad1f08430  cloakbrowser-linux-arm64.tar.gz
```

The signed manifest (`SHA256SUMS` and `SHA256SUMS.sig`) is attached. The wrapper verifies its Ed25519 signature and each archive's SHA-256 checksum automatically.

## CloakBrowser Pro: Stable advances to Chromium 155.0.8059.39.1 (all platforms)

Chromium `155.0.8059.39.1` is now Stable on **Linux** (x64 and ARM64), **Windows** (x64), and **macOS** (Apple Silicon and Intel).

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

### What's new

- **The newest Chromium, 155**, on every platform.
- **Windows and macOS catch up with Linux:** safer proxy handling, the more patient license connection with the `--license-route` flag, and the refined Windows persona.
- **Closer to real Chrome everywhere:** graphics checks, canvas exports, network timing, the reported CPU architecture on ARM hosts, and a few more Windows font names all behave the way real Chrome does on real hardware.
- **DNS that follows your proxy:** with `--fingerprint-transparent-proxy`, sites are resolved with Cloudflare's DNS over HTTPS, sent through your proxy. Use your own with `--fingerprint-transparent-proxy-dns=<url>`, or `local` for the old behavior.
- **Clear license errors everywhere**, a **more stable macOS persona**, **quieter Windows security logs**, and a **smaller Linux download**.

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

### Current wrapper: v0.6.3

Update the wrapper before launching:

```bash
pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.6.3
```

### Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Stable build for your platform:

```bash
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.2   # Linux
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.1   # Windows, macOS
```

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

**If you hit a regression, please tell us.** [Open an issue](https://github.com/CloakHQ/CloakBrowser/issues) or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.
